title.narrative: Shelter Support for Earthquake-Affected Communities in Chapa Dara District, Kunar Province, Afghanistan (2025–2026)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aims to provide cash-for-shelter assistance to earthquake-affected and vulnerable households in Bastalla, Watala, Sayed Khail, Warsak, Sanzaye, Nakora and Kanday areas of Chapa Dara District, Kunar Province. The intervention will reach 286 households, equivalent to 2,002 individuals, including 452 women, 529 girls, 469 men and 552 boys. Of the total caseload, 50 households will be women-headed households, and approximately 16 percent of individuals reached will be persons with disabilities, in line with recognized humanitarian standards for disability inclusion.ltbrgtAll targeted households have been significantly affected by the recent earthquake and will receive shelter support through a tiered cash-for-shelter approach based on the level of damage and household needs. The project will provide transitional shelter assistance to 152 households, major shelter repair support to 129 households and minor repair assistance to 5 households. The cash values will be USD 3,767.10 for transitional shelter, USD 550 for major repairs and USD 330 for minor repairs.ltbrgtThe project will follow national Cash Working Group procedures and ES/NFI Cluster guidance to ensure transparent, safe and accountable delivery. Cash assistance will be disbursed in two to three instalments, with each tranche subject to verification of construction or repair progress by IRW project, MEAL and finance teams. This phased approach will support appropriate use of funds and ensure that shelter works are completed in line with agreed technical standards, safety considerations and project objectives.ltbrgtCash transfers will be facilitated through a Money Service Provider selected through a competitive procurement process to ensure transparency and value for money. Following beneficiary identification and verification by IRW programme and MEAL teams, and in coordination with relevant local stakeholders, safe and accessible distribution sites will be selected. Distribution arrangements will consider access for women, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.ltbrgtThe MSP will deliver cash to designated distribution points and disburse assistance only to verified beneficiaries. Prior to engagement, the MSP will sign IRW’s Data Protection and Safeguarding Framework, committing to confidentiality, dignity and protection of the communities served. The MSP service fee will be 1.25 percent.ltbrgtBeneficiaries will be selected using vulnerability criteria, with priority given to women-headed households, persons with disabilities, girls, older persons and other at-risk groups, in line with Cluster guidance. Information on the complaints and feedback mechanism, including hotline numbers, will be shared during distributions and printed on beneficiary tokens. IRW will maintain a functional CFM system and coordinate closely with relevant authorities and the ES/NFI Cluster.ltbrgtThe project will adhere to the Do No Harm principle, ensuring that assistance is delivered in a safe, dignified, inclusive and accountable manner throughout implementation. ltbrgtlt/pgt
